landing_title: An ancient invitation. One chance to answer.
landing_lede: Light Delay is a first-contact thriller about a human crew crossing an ancient throat near Jupiter to meet the civilization that built it.
landing_about_body: The Velari waited thousands of years for humanity to find their door. Some read that patience as restraint; others see a threat. A hidden act of sabotage turns that disagreement into a race to preserve first contact.

studio_qwen_help_intro: Practical order: (1) line direction, (2) prefix or default if needed, (3) temperature in small steps, (4) top-p and top-k if chaotic or flat, (5) repetition penalty only for loops. Max tokens only for length cutoffs. The model does not “feel” emotion: the instruct describes it; numeric knobs only open or close variation.
studio_help_temperature:
Scales the probability distribution before sampling the next audio token. Low (~0.3–0.6): stable, little colour. Mid (~0.75–0.9): dual baseline. High (~1.0–1.3): more performance and risk; above ~1.3 often hurts intelligibility.

To hunt emotion: raise by 0.05–0.1 from 0.82 and regenerate the same line. If it sounds drunk, metallic, or invents syllables, lower it. Does not replace a good instruct.
studio_help_top_p:
Nucleus sampling: at each step only the smallest set of tokens whose cumulative mass ≥ p is kept. Combines with temperature.

Low (0.5–0.75): rigid. 0.9: default. Near 1.0: almost no cut.

If high temperature is chaotic, lower top-p (e.g. 0.8). If mid temperature sounds robotic, raise toward 0.95–1.0.
studio_help_top_k:
Hard cap: only the k most likely tokens may be sampled. k=1 is greedy. Combines with top-p and temperature.

Low (5–20): very deterministic. 50: default. High (80–100): more nuance when temp and top-p are permissive.

For varied takes of the same line, raise k with a bit of temperature. If each take swings tempo or accent too much, lower k (20–30).
studio_help_max_tokens:
Cap on audio/code tokens for this generation. Does not control emotion or speed: only how long the take can run. The worker also rejects outputs over 25 s.

Raise only if you hear an abrupt end cut. Do not use it to “add expression”. If it still cuts at 3072, check text and instruct (slow pace lengthens a lot).
studio_help_repetition:
Discourages repeating recent patterns (syllables, fillers, loops). Does not add emotion.

~1.0: none. 1.05: default. 1.1–1.2: stronger against loops. >1.2 can sound choppy.

If you hear repeats or unfinished endings: 1.08–1.15. If it sounds clipped or skips words: lower to 1.0–1.03.
studio_help_line_instruct:
Per-line performance note (pressure, rhythm, relationship, subtext). Merged with the expressiveness prefix.

This is the semantic emotion control. Write in English acting direction (the TTS instruct path is tuned that way). Ask how it is said, not what the plot means.

Change this first; regenerate with fixed knobs to hear the instruct’s range.
studio_help_expressiveness:
Short template prepended to the line direction when not already present. ES asks for emotional colour and softened L1 accent; EN for dynamics without flattening. Also asks to finish every syllable.

Sets the delivery floor; does not replace line direction. If everything is flat, strengthen here. If ES accent becomes cartoonish, keep “soften the accent”.
studio_help_default_instruct:
Language-level base instruct when there is no useful line direction, or as the compose anchor. Defines empty-scene behaviour.

Not the character profile (that lives in the ref WAV). If the line already has instruct, the default matters less than the final compose.
